writer: workstream B (the platinum publisher, reporting-publish/publisher.py build_client_summary)
reader: the Performance page, through the reporting read route's client summary operation
authored_under: IRPT_DASHBD.TO-DB-b-16 under CTO RULINGS batch 197 (@7563d60e68) (a): the per-client summary gets its own versioned contract, because a per-client summary is a different GRAIN from a per-account manifest (rule 24 ii: one grain per schema)

address.key_shape: platinum/reporting/client=<client_id>/summary.json beneath the firm's irpt prefix; the key is builder output (publisher.summary_address), never a typed key (rule 30)
address.client_id: the ISSUED opaque client id (cli_ + 24 hex) of a directory entry; never a name and never a custodian number

change_rule: C-SEAM: workstream B is the only writer of this file and the page is its only reader. A field the page needs and the file lacks is a change request to the issuer of workstream B, never a page-side derivation from another source. The per-account series and manifest are a different grain with their own contract; this file never restates them.
read_rule: The read route serves summary.json ONLY when the viewer's scope covers EVERY account the document names (accounts[].account_id and unpublished_account_ids), each tested with the per-account coverage check the account route uses. A client id in a request is a claim, never a grant: partial coverage, a document of another firm or of another client is refused OBJECT_NOT_COVERED with no bytes; an absent summary is NOT_READY and the page falls back to per-account manifests.

summary.shape: one JSON object per directory client with at least one published account; ids only, no name and no custodian account number

client_id.sentence: The issued opaque client id the document is keyed by; never null.

firm.sentence: The registry-derived firm scope all the named accounts belong to; never null and never a typed token.

as_of.sentence: The newest as_of among the per-account entries, as YYYY-MM-DD; each account's own as_of rides in its entry; never null.

windows.sentence: The standard windows computed for every account entry, in order: YTD, QTD, 1Y, 3Y, SI; never null.

accounts.sentence: One entry per PUBLISHED account of the client, sorted by account_id; never null and never empty (a client with no published account has no summary).

unpublished_account_ids.sentence: The client's account ids that have no published series, sorted, so a summary never reads as the whole client when it is not; an empty list when every account is published, never null.

built_at.sentence: When the publisher built the document, as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp; never null.

publisher_version.sentence: The version string of the publisher code that wrote the document; never null.

account_id.sentence: The issued opaque account id of one published account of the client; the id space the viewer's scope is tested in; never null.

as_of.sentence: The last data day of that account's series, equal to the series file's as_of; never null.

first_data_date.sentence: The first data day of that account's series, equal to the series file's first_data_date; never null.

series_object.sentence: The name of the account's series object (series.json.gz) the page fetches for the full history; never null.

windows.sentence: A map from each window in `windows` to the geometric link of the account's daily total return over that window as a decimal fraction (0.01 is one percent), or null; null exactly where window_status is not MEASURED, and a partial link is never returned.

window_status.sentence: A map from each window in `windows` to one member of the `window_status` enum below, saying why the figure is what it is; never null.

window_status.domain: why one account's figure for one standard window is what it is; one value per (account, window) in summary.accounts[].window_status

meanings.MEASURED: the series spans the window and every day in it has a return; the figure is the geometric link of those days
meanings.NOT_SPANNED: the series starts after the window's opening anchor, so the window has days with no prior day behind them; the figure is null and is never a partial link
meanings.BREAK: a day inside the window carries a null return; the link breaks there and is never bridged; the figure is null

window_status.source: reporting-publish/publisher.py WINDOW_MEASURED, WINDOW_NOT_SPANNED, WINDOW_BREAK, returned by window_return()

four_postulate_record.i: MECE over a declared domain: the domain is the (account, window) pair, and window_return() takes exactly one of three branches in order - first_data_date after the anchor is NOT_SPANNED; else a null return day in the window is BREAK; else MEASURED - so every pair has exactly one value and the three are disjoint; a figure is non-null if and only if the value is MEASURED. The uncovered member was hunted by subtraction: the three return statements of window_return() are the whole population of outcomes (3 of 3), and the builder's fixture has no pair outside them.
four_postulate_record.ii: Same grain: every value describes one window of one account (the grain of accounts[].window_status[<window>]); none describes the client, the account as a whole or a day. The day-level state lives in the series contract's day_quality at a finer grain and is not restated here.
four_postulate_record.iii: Intent coherence: one axis, one intent - 'can the window's figure be given, and if not why'. NOT_SPANNED is an absence of history before the window and BREAK is an absence of a return inside it; neither is a data-quality grade of a day, which is day_quality's intent.
four_postulate_record.iv: State coherence: a figure exists only under MEASURED; NOT_SPANNED and BREAK both hold a null and differ in remedy (NOT_SPANNED clears when the window ages into the series, BREAK clears only when the missing day is published); neither is moved by the other remedy. The token MEASURED is also a member of day_quality in the daily contract: that is a different field at a different grain, and a consumer keys on the field, never on the bare token.

token_census.method: git grep -I -o -w -e <token> over the tracked tree at the worker's base 713110dbeb, 2026-10-02; -w is the word boundary, so NOT_SPANNED counts as one word and not as SPANNED
token_census.reading: MEASURED and BREAK are common words in the tree (MEASURED is also a day_quality member, hence the field-not-token rule in postulate iv); NOT_SPANNED is specific to this enum; the counts are a collision census, not a usage count of this field
